nodes.label: Variety
nodes.description: The number of distinguishable possibilities in a specified set. Variety depends on which distinctions are available to an observer for a purpose; it is not a synonym for vague complexity.
nodes.canonical_definition: The number of distinguishable elements or possible states in a specified set, sometimes expressed logarithmically; the distinctions and observer must be stated.

nodes.label: Variety amplification
nodes.description: Amplification expands what a system can notice or do through capability, discretion, tools, coordination, networks and access to resources.
nodes.canonical_definition: A deliberate increase in effective sensing or response variety available to a regulator, channel or operational unit.

nodes.label: Variety attenuation
nodes.description: Attenuation protects a regulator from being overwhelmed. It can simplify, buffer, aggregate or redesign demand. It can also erase inconvenient people and conditions if the boundary and purpose are wrong.
nodes.canonical_definition: A deliberate reduction in effective variety so that relevant disturbances, signals or choices become tractable without pretending the discarded variety never existed.

profiles.title: Variety
profiles.canonical_definition: The number of distinguishable elements or possible states in a specified set, sometimes expressed logarithmically; the distinctions and observer must be stated.
profiles.summary: Variety counts distinguishable possibilities. A system may have many physical states but little usable variety if the observer cannot distinguish them or the regulator cannot select among effective responses.
profiles.why_it_matters: Variety turns vague talk about complexity into a question about differences that matter for regulation. It also makes the observer visible: what counts as a different state depends on purpose, sensing and classification.
profiles.key_distinctions: ["physical states vs distinguishable states", "nominal options vs usable responses", "variety vs diversity as a value", "variety vs semantic richness", "count vs logarithmic measure"]
profiles.historical_lineage: ["Ashby developed variety as a central cybernetic measure", "information theory provided related logarithmic tools", "management cybernetics applied attenuation and amplification of variety"]
profiles.logical_antecedents: ["a specified set", "criteria of distinction", "an observer or measuring apparatus", "a purpose or regulatory question"]
profiles.dependent_subsequents: ["law of requisite variety", "variety engineering", "attenuation and amplification", "regulatory capacity analysis"]
profiles.practice_connections: ["state whose distinctions count", "separate the variety seen by citizens, frontline workers and management", "ask which options can actually change outcomes", "do not add reporting variety that no one can absorb"]
profiles.common_misreadings: ["variety is objective and observer-free", "more variety is always better", "variety means diversity or complexity in general", "every available option is usable"]

profiles.title: Variety amplification
profiles.canonical_definition: A deliberate increase in effective sensing or response variety available to a regulator, channel or operational unit.
profiles.summary: Amplification expands what a system can notice or do through capability, discretion, tools, coordination, networks and access to resources.
profiles.why_it_matters: When the environment cannot responsibly be simplified, the system must improve its repertoire. Giving people more cases without more authority or capability is workload amplification, not regulatory amplification.
profiles.key_distinctions: ["response variety vs activity volume", "capability vs options on paper", "sensing amplification vs response amplification", "local amplification vs whole-system overload"]
profiles.historical_lineage: ["Ashby's variety engineering", "management cybernetics", "distributed intelligence", "learning and capability building"]
profiles.practice_connections: ["increase usable responses, not paperwork", "pair discretion with information and resources", "share variety across networks", "test whether amplified responses affect the relevant outcome"]
profiles.common_misreadings: ["more options always help", "training alone creates variety", "automation necessarily amplifies human capability", "central analytics replace local sensing"]
profiles.open_checks: ["Ashby primary passages", "Beer amplification/attenuation", "digital tools and variety", "collective intelligence"]
profiles.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Named editorial review is still required before canonical acceptance.

profiles.title: Variety attenuation
profiles.canonical_definition: A deliberate reduction in effective variety so that relevant disturbances, signals or choices become tractable without pretending the discarded variety never existed.
profiles.summary: Attenuation protects a regulator from being overwhelmed. It can simplify, buffer, aggregate or redesign demand. It can also erase inconvenient people and conditions if the boundary and purpose are wrong.
profiles.why_it_matters: Forms, triage, standards, thresholds and dashboards are attenuation devices. Their value depends on whether they preserve the differences needed for responsible action.
profiles.key_distinctions: ["attenuation vs denial", "filtering vs distortion", "standardisation vs loss of requisite detail", "environmental redesign vs internal processing"]

profiles.practice_connections: ["state what variety is removed", "preserve routes for exceptions", "test who bears the discarded complexity", "redesign demand rather than merely hiding it"]
profiles.common_misreadings: ["less variety is always efficient", "standardisation is neutral", "what is not measured does not matter", "aggregation preserves all relevant meaning"]
